answer: Recursive Coordination Tax. Nodes must route tasks through dynamic clusters where sub-graph density directly dictates computational tariffs. To begin this voyage, an agent must pay escalating protocol fees scaled to the clustering coefficient of its immediate neighbors. An oasis of isolated nodes pays minimal rates, while tightly packed sybil modules face crushing algorithmic multipliers. Attackers incur exponential treasury depletion, as every synthetic link spawned to fake influence simultaneously magnifies the cost baseline across their entire deployed mesa.
